learn.hook: Class 5 did a survey: how do you come to school? Let's be data detectives and find the story in the numbers!
points: Tally marks are drawn in bundles of 5 (four lines and one across) to count quickly.
From data we can find the most, the least, the total and the difference.
We can also find fractions of the data: 20 out of 40 is half.
Only say what the data really shows. Do not guess things it does not tell.

example.q: 40 children answered: 20 walk, 12 come by bus, 8 cycle. What fraction walk? How many more walk than cycle?
example.answer: Half walk; 12 more walk than cycle

learn.reallife: Schools, shops and doctors collect data to make good decisions.

games.title: Data: dogs 10, cats 6, fish 4
buckets: Can be answered from the data
items: How many more dogs than cats?
Which pet is the least common?

items.q: Bars of 12 and 7: how many more?

quiz.q: A tally shows two bundles of five and 3 more lines. What number is that?
40 children were asked how they come to school. 20 walk. What fraction of the children walk?
quiz.mistake: Writes the number who walk over the number who don't (20/20)

quiz.q: In the same survey, 20 children walk and 8 cycle. How many more walk than cycle?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Temperatures this week: Mon 30°, Tue 32°, Wed 29°, Thu 33°. Which day was the hottest?
quiz.explain: 33° is the highest, so Thursday was the hottest.

quiz.q: Favourite part of Diwali: Sweets 15, Diyas 12, Rangoli 9, Lights 4. Which statement is TRUE?
options: Lights are more popular than Diyas
Rangoli and Diyas got the same votes
quiz.explain: 15 is the biggest number, so Sweets got the most votes.

quiz.q: In that Diwali survey (15, 12, 9 and 4 votes), how many children voted in all?
Books read this month: Riya 5, Arjun 8, Meena 6, Kabir 5. How many children read more than 5 books?
quiz.explain: Arjun (8) and Meena (6) read more than 5. Riya and Kabir read exactly 5, which is not more than 5.
quiz.mistake: Counts children who read exactly 5 as 'more than 5'

quiz.q: In a quiz, Team A scored 45 and Team B scored 60. By how many points did Team B win?

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What can we learn from a table of numbers?'
teach.praise: Wow! Data tells us the most, the least, the total and how many more. I'm a data detective now!
teach.nudge: What questions can I answer from the numbers? Can I find the biggest and the total?

learn.hook: Can one little mango picture stand for 5 mangoes? In a pictograph, it can!
points: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols.
The key tells how many things one symbol stands for, like 🥭 = 5 mangoes.
To read it, multiply the number of symbols by the key.
Half a symbol stands for half the key number.
Choose a key that keeps the pictures easy to draw and count.

example.q: Key: 🍎 = 10 apples. A shop's row shows 🍎🍎🍎🍎 and half an 🍎. How many apples?

learn.reallife: Pictographs are used in newspapers, school charts and posters to show data in a fun way.

items.text: Half a ☀️ stands for ___ sunny day

quiz.q: Key: 🍎 = 10 apples. A shop's row shows 🍎🍎🍎🍎. How many apples does the shop have?
quiz.mistake: Counts the symbols but forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: ⭐ = 4 children. A row shows 3 and a half ⭐. How many children is that?
quiz.explain: 3 stars = 12 children. Half a star = 2 children. 12 + 2 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the half symbol, or counts it as a full one

quiz.q: Key: 🏏 = 10 runs. Kabir has 🏏🏏🏏🏏🏏🏏 and Joseph has 🏏🏏🏏. How many more runs did Kabir score?
quiz.mistake: Gives the difference in symbols (3) and forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: 🙂 = 5 children. How many 🙂 are needed to show 35 children?
quiz.mistake: Draws one symbol for each child

quiz.q: Why does a pictograph have a key?
options: So we know how many each symbol stands for
quiz.explain: Without the key we cannot tell if one symbol means 1, 5 or 10 things.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the symbols always mean 1 each

quiz.q: Key: 📚 = 20 books. The library row shows 📚📚 and half a 📚. How many books?
A pictograph will show 200, 350 and 500 visitors at a mela. Which key is the best choice?
quiz.explain: With 50, the rows need 4, 7 and 10 symbols. Easy to draw and read!
quiz.mistake: Picks a key that needs hundreds of symbols or does not divide the numbers

quiz.q: Key: 🌸 = 6 flowers. Meena picked 24 flowers. How many 🌸 symbols show this?
quiz.mistake: Uses the key number as the answer

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'In a pictograph, how do I know how many things one picture means?'
teach.praise: Yay! Read the key, then multiply the symbols by it. Easy-peasy!
teach.nudge: What part of the pictograph tells me what a symbol is worth? What do I do then?

topics.title: Two-wheelers on the road: pictographs with a scale

learn.hook: Students counted two-wheelers passing their school in 15 minutes. Each 🛵 stands for 3 vehicles!
points: With the scale 🛵 = 3 vehicles, multiply the number of icons by 3.
Pictograph (🛵 = 3 vehicles): Scooters 🛵×6, Motorcycles 🛵×8, Mopeds 🛵×4, E-scooters 🛵×2.
So scooters = 6 × 3 = 18, motorcycles = 24, mopeds = 12, e-scooters = 6. The maximum is motorcycles.
Total = 18 + 24 + 12 + 6 = 60 vehicles. Difference: motorcycles − mopeds = 24 − 12 = 12.
To redraw with 🛵 = 6 vehicles, divide each value by 6: 3, 4, 2 and 1 icons.

example.q: Using the pictograph, how many more motorcycles than scooters passed?

learn.reallife: Traffic police count vehicles at busy crossings to plan signals and lanes.

quiz.q: Pictograph (🛵 = 3 vehicles): Scooters 🛵×6, Motorcycles 🛵×8, Mopeds 🛵×4, E-scooters 🛵×2. How many scooters passed?
quiz.mistake: Counts icons instead of using the scale

quiz.q: In the two-wheeler pictograph (🛵 = 3), which type passed most often?
quiz.explain: Motorcycles have the most icons, 8, which is 24 vehicles.

quiz.q: Using 🛵 = 3, how many motorcycles passed (8 icons)?
What is the total number of two-wheelers (6, 8, 4 and 2 icons; 🛵 = 3)?
How many more motorcycles (8 icons) than mopeds (4 icons) passed, with 🛵 = 3?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts icons and forgets the scale

quiz.q: If the same data is redrawn with 🛵 = 6, how many icons show the 24 motorcycles?
quiz.mistake: Keeps the old number of icons

quiz.q: With 🛵 = 6, how many icons show the 6 e-scooters?
Why might we choose 🛵 = 6 instead of 🛵 = 3?
options: To change the real number of vehicles
To draw fewer icons for big numbers
quiz.explain: A bigger scale needs fewer icons; the data stays the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a new scale changes the data

teach.ask: Gappu drew 5 🛵 icons with the key 🛵 = 3. How many vehicles is that? And how many icons with 🛵 = 5?
teach.praise: 5 × 3 = 15 vehicles. With 🛵 = 5 I need only 3 icons!
teach.nudge: What does each icon stand for?

learn.hook: Asha and Ravi both have 24 hours a day. How differently do they spend them?
points: A table or a picture record can show how much time someone spends on each activity.
Asha: sleep 9 h, school 7 h, play 2 h, study 2 h, TV 1 h, meals 1 h 30 min, other 1 h 30 min. Ravi: sleep 8 h, school 7 h, play 1 h, study 2 h, TV 4 h, meals 1 h, other 1 h.
To compare, find the difference for each activity: Ravi watches TV 4 − 1 = 3 hours more than Asha.
The times in a full day must add up to 24 hours.
A balanced routine has enough sleep, play and study, and not too much screen time.

example.q: How much more does Asha sleep than Ravi?

learn.reallife: Doctors say children your age need about 9–11 hours of sleep and some active play every day.

games.title: Compare the routines
items: Ravi watches 3 hours more TV than Asha.
The table shows 7 h for both.
Asha's activities add up to 24 hours.

quiz.q: Asha watches TV for 1 hour a day and Ravi for 4 hours. How many more hours does Ravi watch?
How much more does Asha sleep than Ravi (9 h and 8 h)?
Who plays more, and by how much (Asha 2 h, Ravi 1 h)?
Ravi's times: sleep 8, school 7, play 1, study 2, TV 4, meals 1, other 1 (hours). What is the total in hours?
On which activity do Asha and Ravi spend the same time?
quiz.explain: Both spend 7 h at school and 2 h studying.

quiz.q: Whose routine is more balanced?
options: Asha's — more sleep and play, less TV
quiz.explain: Asha sleeps more, plays more and watches less TV.
quiz.mistake: Thinks more TV time is better

quiz.q: Asha spends 1 h 30 min on meals and Ravi spends 1 h. How many more minutes does Asha spend?
If Ravi cuts his TV time by 2 hours and adds it to play, how many hours does he play?
quiz.mistake: Takes the time away from play too

teach.ask: Gappu sleeps 6 hours and watches the sky-TV for 5 hours. His friend sleeps 10 hours and watches 1 hour. Whose day is more balanced?
teach.praise: My friend sleeps more and watches less TV, so my friend's day is more balanced!
teach.nudge: Who gets more sleep and less screen time?

topics.title: A day in my life as a bar graph

learn.hook: Turn your whole day into bars! The longest bar shows what you do most.
points: Record your 24-hour routine in hours and minutes. Check that it adds up to 24 hours.
To draw a bar graph: draw two axes, write the activities along one, mark a scale (like 1 square = 1 hour) along the other.
Draw each bar as long as its time. Keep bars the same width with equal gaps.
Strip graph: cut paper strips as long as each measured length (like index fingers) and paste them side by side — it becomes a bar graph.
Give the graph a title and label both axes.

example.q: Meena's day: sleep 10 h, school 6 h, play 2 h, homework 2 h, meals 2 h, other ? Find 'other'.

learn.reallife: Health apps show your sleep and exercise as bars every day.

games.title: Draw a bar graph
items: Collect the data in a table
Draw the two axes and mark a scale
Draw a bar of the right length for each item
Check each bar against the table

items.q: Sleep 10 h, scale 1 square = 1 h: squares?
School 6 h, scale 1 square = 2 h: squares?
Bar of 4 squares, 1 square = 30 min: minutes?

quiz.q: Meena's day: sleep 10 h, school 6 h, play 2 h, homework 2 h, meals 2 h and other. How many hours is 'other'?
In Meena's bar graph, which activity has the longest bar?
With the scale 1 square = 1 hour, how many squares long is the bar for 6 hours of school?
With the scale 1 square = 2 hours, how many squares show 10 hours of sleep?
Children paste paper strips as long as their index fingers: Ali 6 cm, Bina 5 cm 5 mm, Chetan 6 cm 2 mm. Whose strip is longest?
quiz.explain: 6 cm 2 mm = 62 mm is the longest.

quiz.q: In that strip graph, whose finger is shortest?
quiz.explain: 5 cm 5 mm = 55 mm is the shortest.

quiz.q: What must all the bars in a bar graph have the same?
quiz.explain: Only the lengths change; widths stay equal so the graph is fair.

quiz.q: A bar for homework is 3 squares long and each square is 30 minutes. How long is homework?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to draw a bar graph of his day. What do I need to remember?
teach.praise: I choose a scale, keep bars the same width, and add a title and labels!
teach.nudge: What makes a bar graph easy to read?

learn.hook: Which fruit does your class love most? A bar graph shows the winner in one look!
points: A bar graph uses bars of different lengths to show data.
The longer or taller the bar, the bigger the number it shows.
The scale on the side tells what each line stands for, like 1 line = 2 children.
All bars should be the same width with equal gaps between them.
Bars can go up (vertical) or across (horizontal).

example.q: On a bar graph each line stands for 2 children. The Mango bar reaches 6 lines. How many children chose mango?

learn.reallife: Cricket scorecards on TV, rainfall charts and school results often use bar graphs.

games.title: Fewest to most votes
games.prompt: Favourite game votes: Kabaddi 9, Cricket 15, Football 11, Kho-kho 6. Order the bars from shortest to tallest

games.title: True or false?
items: In a bar graph, all bars should be the same width.
Only the length should change, so the graph is fair.
The longest bar shows the smallest number.
The longest bar shows the biggest number.
We need the scale to read the numbers on a bar graph.
The scale tells what each line stands for.
Bars can be drawn going across, not only up.
Horizontal bar graphs work the same way.
If 1 line = 5, a bar 4 lines tall shows 4.

quiz.q: Favourite fruits in Class 5: Mango 12, Banana 8, Apple 5, Grapes 10. Which fruit has the tallest bar?
quiz.explain: Mango has the biggest number, 12, so its bar is tallest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the fruit with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Using the same fruit graph (Mango 12, Banana 8), how many more children chose Mango than Banana?
In the fruit graph (Mango 12, Banana 8, Apple 5, Grapes 10), how many children voted in all?
On a bar graph, each line stands for 2 children. A bar reaches 7 lines. How many children does it show?
quiz.mistake: Reads the number of lines and forgets the scale

quiz.q: Runs in each over: Over 1 = 6, Over 2 = 10, Over 3 = 4, Over 4 = 12. Which over had the most runs?
quiz.explain: Over 4 has the tallest bar with 12 runs.
quiz.mistake: Picks the over with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Using the runs graph (6, 10, 4 and 12 runs), how many runs were scored in all 4 overs?
quiz.mistake: Makes an adding slip or misses one over

quiz.q: Rainy days: June 8, July 15, August 12, September 6. Which month had the fewest rainy days?
quiz.explain: September has the shortest bar, 6 days.
quiz.mistake: Picks the month with the most rain

quiz.q: What does a taller bar on a bar graph tell us?
options: There is more of that thing
There is less of that thing
quiz.explain: Bar height shows the number. Taller means more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the height has no meaning

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I read a bar graph?'
teach.praise: Super! Taller bars mean more, and the scale tells me the exact number!
teach.nudge: What does the height of a bar show? What tells me what each line is worth?

topics.title: Food wastage in the school canteen

learn.hook: Every plate of food left uneaten is food that could have fed someone. A bar graph can show us how much!
points: Food wasted in the canteen (kg): Mon 8, Tue 5, Wed 12, Thu 6, Fri 9.
The tallest bar (Wednesday, 12 kg) shows the most waste; the shortest (Tuesday, 5 kg) shows the least.
Total for the week = 8 + 5 + 12 + 6 + 9 = 40 kg.
Use data in a calculation: if one child eats about 250 g, then 40 kg = 40,000 g could feed 40,000 ÷ 250 = 160 children.
We can predict from data (Wednesday may again be high) and think of ways to reduce waste: take smaller servings, ask for more if hungry, share extra food.

example.q: Wednesday's waste was 12 kg. If one child eats about 250 g, how many children could that feed?

learn.reallife: Many schools now weigh leftover food to help children waste less.

games.title: Helps reduce food waste?
items: Ask for more only if hungry
Fill the plate and leave half
Throw away food you did not touch
Tell the canteen which dishes are not liked

items.q: Children fed by 40 kg at 250 g each

quiz.q: Food wasted in the canteen (kg): Mon 8, Tue 5, Wed 12, Thu 6, Fri 9. On which day was the most food wasted?
quiz.explain: Wednesday's bar is the tallest, 12 kg.

quiz.q: Using the canteen data, on which day was the least food wasted?
quiz.explain: Tuesday's bar is the shortest, 5 kg.

quiz.q: What is the total food wasted in the week (8, 5, 12, 6, 9 kg)?
How much more food was wasted on Wednesday (12 kg) than on Thursday (6 kg)?
If one child eats about 250 g, how many children could the week's 40 kg feed?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change kg to g

quiz.q: Wednesday is always the day khichdi is served, and most waste happens then. What is a sensible prediction?
options: Next Wednesday may also have high waste
Next Wednesday will have no waste
Tuesday will have the most waste
quiz.explain: Patterns in data help us predict, though we cannot be certain.

quiz.q: Which is the best way to reduce food waste in the canteen?
options: Take a small serving and ask for more if still hungry
Fill the plate as much as possible
Throw away food that is not tasty
quiz.explain: Taking only what you can eat means less is thrown away.
quiz.mistake: Picks an idea that increases waste

quiz.q: What is the average (equal share) of food wasted per day over the 5 days (40 kg total)?

teach.ask: Gappu's canteen wasted 3 kg on Monday and 7 kg on Tuesday. What can the graph tell me, and how can we waste less?
teach.praise: Tuesday wasted most, 10 kg in all. We can take smaller servings and share!
teach.nudge: Which day had the taller bar, and what could we change?

topics.title: True or false? Observing a picture

learn.hook: Look carefully at a busy picture and count. Then be a judge: is each statement true or false?
points: Count each kind of item in the picture carefully. Make a quick tally if it helps.
A picture of a park shows: 5 children on swings, 3 dogs, 8 birds, 2 benches, 4 trees and 1 ice-cream cart.
Compare counts to check statements: 'There are more birds than dogs' is true because 8 > 3.
Some statements are opinions ('The park is beautiful') — they cannot be checked by counting.
Only say what the picture really shows.

example.q: Is 'There are twice as many trees as benches' true?

learn.reallife: Detectives and reporters observe carefully and check facts before they write.

games.title: Look at the park picture
items: There are more birds than children.
There are more trees than benches.
There are as many dogs as benches.

games.title: Fact or opinion?
items: The park is the best park
There are more trees than benches

quiz.q: A picture of a park shows: 5 children on swings, 3 dogs, 8 birds, 2 benches, 4 trees and 1 ice-cream cart. Which statement is true?
options: There are more dogs than children
There are more birds than dogs

quiz.q: In the park picture, how many more birds than dogs are there?
In the park picture, is 'There are twice as many trees as benches' true?
How many animals (dogs and birds) are in the park picture?
Which statement about the park picture is an opinion, not a fact?
options: The park is the prettiest in town
quiz.explain: 'Prettiest' is what someone feels; it cannot be counted.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every statement can be checked

quiz.q: In the park picture, is 'There are fewer children than trees' true?
quiz.explain: 5 children and 4 trees: there are more children.

quiz.q: If each bench seats 3 people, how many people can sit on the benches in the park picture?
How many things are in the park picture altogether (children, dogs, birds, benches, trees, cart)?

teach.ask: Gappu looked at a picture with 6 cats and 4 mice and said 'There are more mice.' How do I check?
teach.praise: 6 cats and 4 mice — there are more cats! My statement was false.
teach.nudge: How many of each are in the picture?
